question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode in agent-core, and must that wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy instead of repairing a narrow broken contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on the related tool-classification work or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before implementing early execution.

options.title: Defer Runtime Change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide early tool execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for streaming scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent runtime extraction and agent-core/provider stream fixes make this the strongest available routing signal for the product/runtime decision.
